subject.title: OpenAI Codex profiles need loopback proxy routing

question: Should OpenClaw permit a per-profile, loopback-only proxy endpoint for ChatGPT/Codex OAuth catalog and Responses traffic while retaining the standard `openai/<model>` provider identity?
rationale: This changes where bearer or OAuth-derived requests are sent and adds a new configuration surface; code review cannot determine the intended trust model, supported loopback forms, or long-term operator contract without maintainer direction.

options.title: Approve a narrow loopback sidecar contract
options.body: Allow a strictly validated local endpoint only for the OAuth Responses path, retain current defaults and API-key routing, and require focused rejection and coexistence coverage.

options.title: Require an external provider integration
options.body: Keep the bundled OpenAI provider unchanged and ask deployments to expose this behavior through an external plugin or provider boundary instead.

options.title: Defer pending a broader credential-broker design
options.body: Pause the feature until maintainers define a reusable local credential-broker contract rather than introducing a route-specific setting.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow loopback sidecar contract
recommendation.body: Allow a strictly validated local endpoint only for the OAuth Responses path, retain current defaults and API-key routing, and require focused rejection and coexistence coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository-member author supplied the concrete deployment model and is the available routing contact in the issue context.
